description: Stone-clad thane - turns every blow dodged into Rage and speeds up the longer the fight runs.
_source_note: Rebuilt 5 Nov 2026 from data/reference/coa/primalist.json (41 real CoA Mountain King talents, role TANK, 'Enhancement Shaman'). Replaces a 22-node tree of 14 pure scalars and 2 procs, most of the scalars 5 ranks of +2-3% armour or threat. The two things the spec is built on were both absent: Earth's Rage, the stacking haste the whole tree keys off, and avoidance as a resource - this engine has on_avoid, on_parry and on_block as real triggers and the old tree used none of them. All 6 unlock nodes are preserved - see tools/qa_abilities_obtainable.py.

nodes.name: Unyielding Form
nodes.description: Increases your parry and dodge chance by up to 3%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases your parry and dodge chance by 3% and your Armor contribution from mail and plate by 25%.' Armour-by-armour-type is not a key - there is no per-armour-class scaling in this engine - so that half is dropped. Split over CoA's 2 ranks, so a full investment is CoA's 3%. Was armor_pct 6.0, which is neither half of this talent.

nodes.name: Granite Hide
nodes.description: Increases your armor by 3% per rank.
nodes._source: Not a CoA node - kept from the previous tree. A tank tree needs a plain armour pick and this is it; armor_pct takes percentage POINTS.

nodes.name: Earthen Resolve
nodes.description: Increases your threat generation by 3% per rank.
nodes._source: Not a CoA node - kept from the previous tree at 2% -> 3%. Threat is how a tank does its job and this is the only node in the tree that supplies it directly. FRACTION as a talent effect, unlike the status-effect buff version the engine divides by 100.

nodes.name: Seismically Efficient
nodes.description: Seismic Crash generates 5 additional Rage.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Increases the Rage generated from Seismic Crash by 5 and Seismic Spike by 2.' Frontier has no Seismic Spike, so only the Crash half is built. Seismic Crash costs mana and this spec's defensive abilities cost Rage, so this is the bridge between the two halves of a dual-resource class.

nodes.name: Stone Soldier
nodes.description: Increases your attack power by 3% and your chance to hit by 1.5% per rank.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases the damage of your off hand weapon by 30% and your chance to hit by 3%.' Off-hand weapons are not a separate damage source in this engine, so that half becomes general attack power rather than a key that would read as nothing. Hit split over CoA's 2 ranks.

nodes.name: King of the Mountain
nodes.description: Increases your parry, dodge and haste by 15% of your Strength.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Level 20 Passive. Increases your parry, dodge, and haste rating by 15% of your Strength.' All three pairings are live - parry, dodge and haste are all in STAT_CONVERSION_TARGETS and strength is in STAT_CONVERSION_SOURCES. Conversions are FRACTIONS. The previous tree had this at 0.01 per rank over 4 ranks, i.e. 4% against CoA's 15%.

nodes.name: Mountain Hammer
nodes.description: Learn Mountain Hammer. Hurl a hammer that leaves the target reeling.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Throw a hammer at an enemy dealing Physical damage and stunning them for 5 seconds.' Kept from the previous tree, where this unlock was confusingly named Mountain Mover.

nodes.name: Blessed by the Earth
nodes.description: Primal Rush and Quake grant Earth's Rage, increasing your haste by 2% for 3 turns, stacking 5 times.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Damage dealt by Primal Rush and Quake now grant Earth's Rage. Earth's Rage: Increases movement speed by 4% and haste by 2% for 8 seconds, stacking 5 times.' This is the mechanic the rest of the tree keys off and the old tree had no form of it. Movement speed is dropped; haste on a turn meter means acting more often, which is what a ramping tank wants. 8 sec is 3 turns. Status stat_mods multiply by stacks, so 5 stacks is +10 haste.

nodes.name: Quake
nodes.description: Learn Quake. Stomp the ground and slow everything standing on it.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Stomp the ground, dealing Weapon Damage plus Nature damage to enemies within 8 yds and reduces their melee and ranged haste by 20% for 10 sec.' Kept from the previous tree. One of the two Earth's Rage generators, so it has to be learnable at the same depth as Blessed by the Earth.

nodes.name: Spiritbound
nodes.description: Dodging or parrying an attack grants you 5 Rage and brings your Seismic abilities a turn closer to ready.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Avoiding attacks now grants you 5 Rage and reduces the cooldown of your Seismic abilities by -1 sec.' Ports almost exactly: on_avoid is a real trigger, and reset_cooldown with turns:1 knocks one turn off rather than fully resetting. This is the node that makes avoidance a resource instead of just damage the tank did not take.

nodes.name: Mountain Mover
nodes.description: Dodging or parrying an attack grants a stack of Mountain Mover, increasing your parry by 2% for 3 turns, stacking 5 times.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Avoiding an attack grants a stack of Mountain Mover for 10 sec, stacking 5 times. Wildclaw consumes Mountain Mover stacks to cost 10% less Rage per stack.' The consume-for-cost half is not buildable twice over: nothing reads another effect's stack count, and ability cost keys are read through get_talent_effects() which never includes status effects. So the stacks pay out as parry instead - avoidance begetting avoidance - which keeps the snowball CoA is after through a stat a status effect can actually grant. CoA's 5 stacks and 10 sec (3 turns) kept.

nodes.name: Bash
nodes.description: Your weapon swings have a 30% chance to stun the target for a turn.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Your auto attacks have a 30% chance to deal 50% Weapon Damage and stun them for 1 seconds.' is_stun in an apply_effect payload is live (Mage Fire's Impact uses it). CoA's 30% chance kept, with a 2-turn internal cooldown: a 1-turn stun at 30% per swing with no icd would chain-lock a target in a turn-based fight in a way a 1-second stun never does in real time. The extra 50% weapon damage is dropped - the stun is the talent.

nodes.name: Everything's A Nail
nodes.description: Increases the damage of Mountain Hammer by 25% per rank.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Increases the damage of Mountain Hammer by 50%.' Split over 2 ranks at the same ceiling. Replaces the previous tree's Mountain Hammer Mastery, which was 5 ranks of +8%.

nodes.name: Thane's Guidance
nodes.description: Your weapon swings bring Mountain Hammer a turn closer to ready.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Auto attacks now reduce the cooldown of Mountain Hammer by -1 sec.' A second of real-time cooldown is a turn here, so this ports directly. Also carries CoA's Hammer Time! ('your Mountain Hammer now strikes up to 5 enemies'), which is not built: primalist_mountain_hammer is single-target, and no talent key converts an ability to enemy_aoe - aoe_damage only applies to abilities already flagged that way.

nodes.name: Quakeformer
nodes.description: Casting Wildclaw or a Seismic ability has a 25% chance to make Quake ready again at once.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Casting Wildclaw and Seismic abilities now has a 25% chance to refresh a charge of Quake.' Charges are cooldowns here, so refreshing one is a full reset. CoA's 25% kept, with a 1-turn internal cooldown so it cannot chain. Quake is an Earth's Rage generator, so this feeds the spec's ramp.

nodes.name: Rock Barrier
nodes.description: Learn Rock Barrier. Wrap yourself in stone that soaks up what gets through.
nodes._source: Kept from the previous tree.

nodes.name: Earthenforged Barrier
nodes.description: Increases the armor Rock Barrier provides by 50% and reduces the cost of your abilities by 15% while it holds.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases the Armor provided by Rock Barrier by 50% and it now reduces the cost of your spells and abilities by -25% for the duration.' The armour half ports exactly. The cost reduction cannot be conditioned on Rock Barrier being active - there is no 'while this buff is up' gate for an effect key - so it is unconditional and cut from 25% to 15% to pay for that. Positive is the reduction direction for _cost_pct. Also carries CoA's Rock Solid ('+5 charges of Rock Barrier'), which charges do not exist to support.

nodes.name: Raging Earth
nodes.description: Quake opens a fissure that burns the ground for 2 turns.
nodes._source: CoA verbatim: 'Your Quake now creates a fissure beneath you that deals an additional Nature damage every 2 sec for 6 seconds.' 6 sec is 2 turns. 'Beneath you' is positional and means nothing here, so the fissure lands on the target instead of on the ground. A proc-applied dot takes a flat potency - there is no 'percentage of attack power' form for apply_effect - so 30 per turn, in line with Frontier's other mid-level dots.

nodes.name: Mountain Thane
nodes.description: Increases your Stamina by up to 5%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases your Stamina by 5% and causes Earth's Rage to stack 1 additional time.' Split over CoA's 2 ranks. The extra Earth's Rage stack is dropped: max_stacks lives on the effect Blessed by the Earth applies, and no key edits a sibling node's payload. stamina_pct takes percentage POINTS.

nodes.name: Tilling the Earth
nodes.description: Increases the chance for Bash to trigger by 3% per rank.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Increases the chance to trigger Bash by 3% and increases your expertise by 5.' Neither half is buildable as written: 'expertise' is read by no engine code, and a talent cannot raise ANOTHER node's proc chance - the chance lives on Bash's own payload. Rerouted to crit on Wildclaw, the auto-attack-adjacent ability Bash hangs off, so the point still buys more out of swinging. Flagged rather than authored as a key that reads as nothing.

nodes.name: Earthen Avatar
nodes.description: Learn Earthen Avatar. Become the mountain for a few turns.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Become an avatar of the earth, increasing your damage dealt and reducing your damage taken by 15%, and increasing your melee haste by 20% for 20 seconds. Immune to stuns, roots, and snares.' Kept from the previous tree.

nodes.name: Call of the Mountain
nodes.description: Increases your parry chance by 5% and reduces the physical damage you take by 5%.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Level 40 Passive. Reaching 5 stacks of Earth's Rage now grants Call of the Mountain: increases your parry chance by 5% and reduces damage taken by -5%.' Nothing reads another effect's stack count, so the gate is dropped and the payout is permanent - the same limit Geomancy's Earthshaping payoffs run into. CoA's numbers kept because they are modest enough to stand unconditionally. NEGATIVE is the reduction direction for physical_damage_taken_pct as a talent effect, which is the opposite of the _cost_pct and _cooldown_pct convention - the previous tree's Steadfast Stance had this right.

nodes.name: Primal Guardian
nodes.description: Taking a heavy blow steels you, increasing your haste and parry by 10% for 3 turns.
nodes._source: CoA: 'When Earthen Avatar, Bearskin or Rock Barrier is removed or expires, you now gain 10% melee haste and parry chance for 15 seconds.' NO TRIGGER FIRES WHEN A BUFF EXPIRES - the trigger list is cast, crit, damage dealt, damage taken, weapon swing, kill, block, avoid and parry, and none of them is 'an effect fell off me'. Rerouted onto taking damage at a 20% chance with a 3-turn internal cooldown, which lands it at roughly the cadence a defensive cooldown expiring would. CoA's two stats and 10% kept; 15 sec is 3 turns.

nodes.name: Terrasurge
nodes.description: Learn Terrasurge. Hurl a globule of earth that strips the target's armour.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Unleash a massive globule of earth at an enemy, dealing Physical damage and reducing their Armor by -50% for 10 sec. Pierces through absorption, deflection, and reflection effects.' Kept from the previous tree. Worth knowing: Geomancy's capstone Heavy Earth buffs Terrasurge, and THIS is the only node in the game that unlocks it - a Geomancer taking that capstone has to reach into this tree for the ability, which is a real cross-spec dependency rather than an oversight.

nodes.name: Mountain Fury
nodes.description: Learn Mountain Fury. Call down the judgement of three hammers.
nodes._source: CoA's Judgement of The Three Hammers: 'While active, dealing direct damage has a 20% chance to hurl 3 hammers over 2 seconds, each dealing Physical damage.' Kept from the previous tree, which already paired this name with that ability. CoA's Mountain Fury is a separate frontal-cone pull that Frontier has no ability for; the cone and the pull are both positional anyway.

nodes.name: Shattering
nodes.description: Your critical strikes sharpen you further, increasing your damage by 1% per stack for 3 turns, stacking 10 times.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Damage dealt by each hammer triggered by Judgment of The Three Hammers now grants you 1% increased critical strike chance and damage for 10 seconds, stacking up to 10 times.' The hammers are an ability's internal proc, not something a talent trigger sees, so this hangs off crits instead. The crit-chance half is dropped and the damage half kept, because stacking both would make it self-feeding. damage_dealt_pct is the status-effect route to a damage multiplier and takes percentage POINTS. CoA's 10 stacks and 1% kept.

nodes.name: Earth Destroyer
nodes.description: Reduces the cooldown of Judgement of the Three Hammers by 10% per rank.
nodes._source: CoA: 'Reduces the cooldown of Mountain Fury by -20 sec and increases the duration by 4 sec.' Routed onto the ability this tree actually unlocks under the Mountain Fury name. Expressed as a percentage because cooldowns are counted in turns here, not seconds. Positive is the reduction direction. The duration half is dropped: ability_*_duration applies to dots and hots, and this is an activated buff window.

nodes.name: Mountain Avatar
nodes.description: At full Earth's Rage you are the mountain - blocking a blow sheds stone that batters everything around you.
nodes._source: CoA's description for this node in the export is a broken template reference ($d2), so there is no tooltip to port and it is built from its name and its position as the tank capstone. on_block is a live trigger this tree otherwise never uses, which makes the capstone reward the thing a Mountain King does more than anyone else: stand in front. splash_damage carries a school, so the shed stone is really Nature damage rather than cosmetic, and the Rage grant keeps it feeding the spec's resource loop. The 'at full Earth's Rage' framing is flavour and deliberately promises no number: nothing reads another effect's stack count, and a description that quoted one would be lying.
